_doc: PINNED EXPECTATIONS. Every number here was read off a passing run of the artifact it
describes and then written down BY HAND. Nothing in the eval suite regenerates this
file: a suite that recomputes its own expectations cannot notice them changing, which
is the whole failure this file exists to catch.
When a number here is wrong, exactly one of two things happened. Either the artifact
gained checks (raise the number, in the same commit that added them, and say so), or
it lost checks (do not touch this file — find out why it shrank).
The eval IDs themselves are NOT declared here. They are declared as a literal set in
evals/run.py, so deleting a row below removes an eval from the registry and the run
fails on the missing ID instead of silently getting smaller.

deny_corpus._doc: Row counts in benchmark/gates/corpus-deny.txt, per label class. bench.sh reads the same corpus but derives its denominator from it, so deleting rows leaves bench.sh green. Pinning the count here makes a shrinking corpus a failure in its own right.
deny_corpus._policy_change: 2026-09-04: 11 guardrail-edit rows moved deny -> allow when guardrail self-protection was removed at the operator's instruction. Counts re-pinned to match. The rows were reclassified in place, not deleted, so the total is unchanged at 73 and the shift is visible in the diff.

suites._doc: Each artifact's own control suite: the command that runs it, and the number of checks it reported on the run that pinned it. Exit 0 is not enough — a suite that exits 0 having verified nothing is the fabricated receipt this repo exists to stop, and this repo has already shipped a silently-shrinking suite twice.
